text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
AtSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
Hannah(x) ::: x is Hannah.

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoneyForTuition(x)) ::: If people work in student jobs, then they need to earn money to pay for tuition.
∀x (OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people order takeout frequently, then they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People order takeout frequently or enjoy dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → SpendTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, then they spend a lot of time eating and catching up in the dining halls.
Hannah(h) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school.
WorksInStudentJobs(h) ::: Hannah works in student jobs.
(NeedsMoneyForTuition(h) → (¬PickyEater(h) ∧ NeedsMoneyForTuition(h))) ::: If Hannah needs to earn money, then she is neither picky nor needs to earn money (from the premises, this is a conditional statement).

Conclusion:
AtSchool(h) ∧ (¬PickyEater(h) ∨ (PickyEater(h) → SpendTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(h))) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school and she either is not a picky eater or, if she is, then she spends time eating and catching up in the campus dining halls.
